images.title: Three ribbons to compare
images.purpose: Set up the question: three ribbons of the same length cut into 6, 8 and 10 equal parts, ready for the child to shade 3/6, 4/8 and 5/10 and compare.
images.composition: Three plain flat ribbons of the same length stacked with wide gaps, left edges lined up, a fraction to the right of each, and one question line below.
images.exact_structure: Top ribbon: cut into 6 equal parts, outlined teal #0072B2, all parts plain white. Middle ribbon: exactly the same length, cut into 8 equal parts, outlined amber #E69F00, all plain. Bottom ribbon: exactly the same length, cut into 10 equal parts, outlined reddish purple #CC79A7, all plain. Left and right edges line up. No part is shaded and no vertical line is drawn. Fraction label at the right end of each ribbon. Question line centred below. Exactly 3 ribbons, 6, 8 and 10 parts.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any shading, the fraction 1/2, a line at the middle, or the word yes anywhere in the frame
images.takeaway: Shade each fraction on ribbons of the same length and compare where the shading ends.
images.description: Three equal ribbons cut into 6, 8 and 10 equal parts, unshaded, labelled 3/6, 4/8 and 5/10, with the question are these equivalent?
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say how many parts they would shade on each ribbon and where each shading would end.

image_decisions.why: Equal ribbons ready to shade give the child a way to check equivalence without revealing the answer.
